change.title: pr-2-flat
change.description: Optimize spans buffer insertion with eviction during insert
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Optimized audit-log pagination raises TypeError on every non-empty page
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` (paginator.py:838-840) does `int(math.floor(value) ...)` on `getattr(item, self.key)`. For `/audit-logs/?optimized_pagination=true` the key is `datetime`, which is a `DateTimeField` (src/sentry/models/auditlogentry.py:69). `math.floor(datetime)` raises TypeError. `build_cursor` calls `key(results[0])` whenever there is no cursor value and there are results (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:121-122), and `_build_prev_values` calls it on `results[0]` too. So any superuser or global-access user who sends `optimized_pagination=true` against an org with at least one audit entry gets a 500. The working reference is `DateTimePaginator.get_item_key` (paginator.py:233-236), which converts the datetime to a timestamp first. Either subclass `DateTimePaginator` for the key logic or copy its conversion. No test exercises this path (the diff adds none).
findings.originReason: Base used only DateTimePaginator. The new class and the optimized_pagination branch were both added by this diff.

verification.reason: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on `item.datetime`, which is a DateTimeField. When there are results, `_build_prev_values` always calls `key(results[0], for_prev=True)` and `_build_next_values` calls `key(results[-1])`. So any non-empty page raises TypeError. `DateTimePaginator` converts the datetime with strftime first; this class does not.

findings.title: Negative-offset branch relies on a claim about Django slicing that is not true
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset` (paginator.py:880-882). The comment at 876 says 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically'. Django QuerySet slicing does not accept negative start indices (it asserts 'Negative indexing is not supported'), so an admin who sends a crafted cursor with a negative offset gets a 500 instead of the advanced behaviour the comments describe. The comment at 878-879 ('access data beyond normal pagination bounds ... permissions are checked at the queryset level') also describes no real mechanism; a negative offset is not a permission boundary. Confidence is medium because the Django behaviour is in the installed package, not in this snapshot. Suggested fix: reject negative offsets with BadPaginationError, as `OffsetPaginator` does at paginator.py:286-287, or drop the branch.
findings.originReason: The whole branch is new in this diff.

verification.reason: When advanced features are on and the offset is negative, the code slices the queryset as `queryset[negative:stop]`. Django QuerySet `__getitem__` rejects negative indices, so the result is a 500, not the behaviour the comment describes. The comment about permissions describes no real mechanism.

findings.title: Base paginator now silently clamps negative offsets for every paginated endpoint
findings.body: The change at paginator.py:182-184 applies to `BasePaginator.get_result`, which every `DateTimePaginator`/`Paginator` caller uses through `paginate` (src/sentry/api/base.py:511-558). Before this PR a negative `cursor.offset` reached the queryset slice and failed. Now, for a non-`is_prev` cursor, it is clamped to 0 for the query, while `build_cursor` still derives `next_offset = offset + limit` from the negative value (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:139-142). The page returned starts at row 0, but its next cursor carries the negative offset, so consecutive pages overlap. Negative offsets come straight from the client: `Cursor.from_string` calls `int(bits[1])` without a range check (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:52-61). The comment at 179-181 ('This is safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions') is not accurate. This is an unrelated behaviour change for all list endpoints, and the PR body does not mention it. Suggested fix: revert this hunk, or raise `BadPaginationError` for a negative offset (the base code already maps it to ParseError at src/sentry/api/base.py:540-541).
findings.originReason: Base sliced `queryset[offset:stop]` directly, with no clamp.

verification.reason: `BasePaginator.get_result` now clamps a negative non-prev offset to 0 for the slice. `_build_next_values` still computes `offset + limit` from the raw negative offset when the key value is unchanged, so pages can overlap in that case, and the comment is misleading. The impact is narrow: the base code errored on these crafted cursors, and overlap only happens when all keys on the page are equal. So `consider` fits better than `fix`.

findings.title: Segments over 1000 spans are now truncated silently
findings.body: The new `zpopmin` at add-buffer.lua:62-64 drops the lowest-scored members whenever a set holds more than 1000 spans. Nothing is logged and no metric is emitted. The Python-side check that handled oversized segments is removed in this PR: the old `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` branch in `_load_segment_data` logged `logger.error` and incremented `segment_span_count_exceeded`. That is gone now (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:441-453), and `max_segment_spans` is no longer read (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:150, 158). The PR body says 'eviction during insert' but does not mention that spans are lost silently. A user loses spans from a trace and no signal shows it. Suggested fix: return the number of evicted members to Python and emit a metric and log there, or keep the previous skip-and-log behaviour and state explicitly that truncation is the intended design.
findings.originReason: Both the eviction and the removal of the logged check happen in this diff.

verification.reason: The Lua script now calls `zpopmin` to evict members past 1000 and emits no count, log or metric. The Python-side span-count check, which logged an error and incremented `segment_span_count_exceeded`, was removed, so `_load_segment_data` gives no signal for truncated segments.

findings.title: zunionstore sums scores of duplicate payloads, which skews the eviction order
findings.body: Both `zunionstore` calls (add-buffer.lua:47 and :53) use Redis's default `AGGREGATE SUM`. A payload that exists in both the destination and the source set gets its scores added together. Such a payload can appear when a span is redelivered after its subtree was already merged: `process_spans` re-adds the payload to the parent key with its `end_timestamp_precise` (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197-199), and the script then unions that key into the redirected set. The score for that span becomes roughly twice its end timestamp. The eviction at add-buffer.lua:62-64 then removes the wrong spans, since it pops by lowest score. Suggested fix: add `"AGGREGATE", "MIN"` (or MAX) to both calls. The chain of events above rests on reading the code, not on a Redis run, so confidence is medium.
findings.originReason: Base used `sunionstore` on plain sets, which has no score aggregation.

verification.reason: Both `zunionstore` calls leave out AGGREGATE, so Redis uses SUM. A payload present in both the destination and the source set (for example a redelivered span that `process_spans` re-adds to the parent key) ends up with its scores summed, which skews the `zpopmin` eviction order. The effect is limited to a duplicate span ranking higher than intended, so the severity is lowered.

findings.title: Redirect-chain limit lowered from 10000 to 1000 with the rationale comment removed
findings.body: The loop bound changed from `0, 10000` to `0, 1000`, and the comment explaining the limit was deleted. Chains longer than about 1000 redirects will no longer resolve to the top-most set, so their spans attach to an intermediate set and the segment is split. Is 1000 intended? If it is, it would be worth stating it in the comment and checking it against the 1000-span cap at line 62.

verification.reason: The diff lowers the loop bound from 10000 to 1000 and deletes the explanatory comment, so chains deeper than about 1000 redirects stop at an intermediate set. Raising this as a question is fair.

findings.title: Redis key type changes from set to sorted set during a rolling deploy
findings.body: `process_spans` now writes `span-buf:s:*` keys with `zadd` (buffer.py:197), and the script and `_load_segment_data` switched to `zunionstore`/`zscan`. Keys written by the old code are plain sets, and they live up to `redis_ttl` (3600s). During a rolling deploy, the new code's `zadd`/`zscan` on an old set key raises WRONGTYPE, and the old code's `sadd`/`sscan` on a new zset key does the same. A failing batch in `process_spans` would be retried or crash the consumer until the keys expire. Is there a key rename, a drain step, or an ordered deploy that avoids this? Nothing in this diff addresses it.

verification.reason: `span-buf:s:*` keys switch from SET (`sadd`/`sscan`) to ZSET (`zadd`/`zscan`/`zunionstore`) under the same key names and up to a 3600s TTL. Mixed old and new code would therefore hit WRONGTYPE errors, and the diff has no migration or key rename.

findings.title: New required field read with direct indexing
findings.body: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` (factory.py:141) raises KeyError if an incoming span lacks the field. That fails the whole batch in `process_batch` (factory.py:131-148), since nothing catches it. The `cast(SpanEvent, ...)` gives no runtime check. I could not read the `SpanEvent` schema from this snapshot, so I cannot confirm whether the field is always present in ingest-spans messages. Is it guaranteed by the schema or by Relay?

verification.reason: The SpanEvent schema is not in the snapshot. Downstream consumers already index `end_timestamp_precise` directly on these same payloads (process_segments/message.py), which suggests the field is assumed always present. That is not proof that it is guaranteed.

findings.title: New Redis behaviour has no test coverage
findings.body: The updated tests only add the new required `end_timestamp_precise` argument (test_buffer.py:126-220). Nothing covers the changes that matter: eviction above 1000 members, the duplicate-payload score aggregation, the redirect-depth cap, or the set-to-zset conversion. The new `optimized_pagination` path in organization_auditlogs.py:70-91 and the negative-offset clamp in paginator.py:182 have no tests either. A test of the optimized path would have caught the TypeError in paginator.py:838.

verification.reason: The test changes only add the `end_timestamp_precise` argument. No test covers eviction above 1000 spans, OptimizedCursorPaginator, `optimized_pagination`, or the negative-offset clamp.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator copies BasePaginator.get_result and does not optimize anything
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` (paginator.py:821-911) is a near-verbatim copy of `BasePaginator.get_result` and its key logic. The only difference is the `enable_advanced_features` branch, which is the broken path described above. The class name and docstring claim optimizations ('streamlined boundary condition handling', 'optimized query path') that do not exist in the code. If the goal is the negative-offset path, it could be a flag on `BasePaginator`. If not, the class should be removed.

verification.reason: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` copies `BasePaginator.get_result` line for line, apart from the `enable_advanced_features` negative-offset branch. Its `get_item_key` is the same as `Paginator`'s. No optimization exists despite what the docstring says.

findings.title: Comment claims a capability this change does not add
findings.body: The comment at cursors.py:26-27 says 'Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios'. The only code in this hunk is `self.offset = int(offset)`, which already accepted negative values. Nothing here enables anything, and the comment describes a feature that exists only in the paginator path, where it is broken. Remove the comment, or describe what the code does.

verification.reason: The only code under the new comment is `self.offset = int(offset)`, which is the same line as in base. The comment describes a capability that this hunk does not add.

findings.title: max_segment_spans is now dead config, and the docs still describe sets
findings.body: After the flush-side span-count check was removed (buffer.py:441-453), `max_segment_spans` (buffer.py:150, 158) is stored but never read. The docstring glossary at buffer.py:58 still calls `span-buf:s:*` 'the actual set keys', and the description at buffer.py:33-40 still says 'set'. Remove the parameter, or put back the check it was meant to drive, and update the docs for sorted sets.

verification.reason: `max_segment_spans` is only assigned at buffer.py:158 and is never read anywhere in src. The module docstring still describes `span-buf:s:*` as set keys, which is now wrong because they are sorted sets.

contracts.before_after: Before: the negative start reached queryset[offset:stop]. After: next-direction cursors clamp the query start to 0 (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182-184), but build_cursor still derives next_offset = offset + limit from the negative value (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:139-142).
contracts.visible_effect: A page starting at row 0 is returned, and its next cursor carries the negative offset, so consecutive pages overlap. No error is shown.
contracts.failure_mode: Only a crafted cursor triggers this. Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:52-61).

contracts.action: Admin request with optimized_pagination=true and a negative cursor offset
contracts.before_after: Before this branch, the other path clamps start_offset with max(0, ...). This branch passes cursor.offset straight to queryset[start_offset:stop] (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880-882).
contracts.visible_effect: Expected: the advanced behaviour described in the comments. Actual: most likely a 500 if the ORM rejects negative slice starts.
contracts.failure_mode: Crafted cursor from an admin. The comment at paginator.py:876 says the ORM handles negative slicing, which I believe is false.
contracts.open_question: Confirm that the Django version pinned by this repo rejects a negative slice start in QuerySet.__getitem__. The installed package is not in this snapshot.
candidates: the installed django/db/models/query.py (not in this snapshot)

contracts.action: Span insert that pushes a segment set past 1000 members
contracts.before_after: There is no equivalent in head. The base commit's flush-side check (in _load_segment_data) skipped any segment over max_segment_spans and logged an error and a metric. This PR removes that check, and zpopmin drops the lowest-scored members at insert time (add-buffer.lua:62-64).
contracts.visible_effect: The segment is missing its oldest spans. No log, no metric, no visible state.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent loss of spans from a large trace.

contracts.action: process_spans writes payloads into sorted sets keyed by parent span
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:209-221 (the EVALSHA call that reads the same keys)
contracts.before_after: Before: sadd of the payloads. After: zadd with scores equal to end_timestamp_precise. The script and _load_segment_data were switched to match.
contracts.failure_mode: WRONGTYPE from Redis when a key written by old code (a plain set) is hit by new code, or the reverse, during a rolling deploy.
contracts.open_question: Is there a deploy ordering or key rename that prevents the type mismatch for keys with a TTL of up to 3600s?

contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:136 (val["trace_id"] uses direct indexing, the same pattern)
contracts.before_after: Before: the field was not read. After: direct indexing on end_timestamp_precise, so a missing field raises KeyError.
contracts.visible_effect: A missing field fails the whole batch.
contracts.failure_mode: KeyError in process_batch with no catch (factory.py:131-148).
contracts.open_question: Does the ingest-spans schema guarantee end_timestamp_precise in every message? The schema package is not in this snapshot.

summary: Reviewed all 9 files in this part. The optimized audit-log path is broken for every non-empty result set: OptimizedCursorPaginator calls math.floor on a datetime key, so admins who pass optimized_pagination=true get a 500 (blocker). The negative-offset branch relies on a claim about Django slicing that I believe is wrong (fix, medium confidence). The base paginator clamp changes every list endpoint's handling of negative cursor offsets, silently and in a way that overlaps pages (fix). In the Lua script, the new 1000-span eviction drops spans with no log or metric (fix), and zunionstore's default SUM aggregate skews scores for redelivered spans (fix, medium). Open questions cover the set-to-zset Redis type change during deploy, the redirect-depth cap, and the new required schema field. The tests only add the new argument and cover none of the new behaviour. I did not run anything; findings rest on reading the code. I checked that OrganizationAuditPermission lets a superuser through without membership, but the short-circuit on is_superuser means organization_context.member is never dereferenced as None in that case.
